A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, Figures 1–2, equations, references, and Appendices A–G. All scientific content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original simulations of random-embedding goodness and preference-score estimation error, displayed in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulation results on embedding goodness and score-estimation error in Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: The linear Generalized Bradley-Terry model with diffusion prior, objective in Equation (4), and diffusion and one-hot embedding constructions are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian-embedding and one-hot-encoding scenarios in Section 5. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 2(a) retains classical GBT and feature-only learning as comparators to the full embedding model. Figure 2(b) retains the same comparison between one-hot-encoding GBT and classical GBT.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same data generation, uniform root law, zero-mean nMSE metric, and experimental settings. Figure 2 still uses A=25 and N=500 in panel (a), and A=20 and D=10 in panel (b).

E4.justification: The identity-concatenation analysis in Figure 1 and the dimension and comparison-count sweeps in Figure 2 are unchanged. No additional ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both Figure 2 captions report 100 seeds for panel (a) and 1000 seeds for panel (b). Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The heatmaps and nMSE plots in Figures 1–2 use identical images. Their reported findings, including improved goodness from identity concatenation and accuracy benefits from informative embeddings, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, derivations, and counterexamples in Sections 2–4 and Appendices A–G are unchanged. Minor equation-spacing differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about generalization with monotonicity guarantees for suitable embeddings and improved accuracy with limited comparison data.

C2.justification: The diffusion interpretation and explanations of experimental trends are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning embedding guarantees and concerns about inhumane preference-data collection.

D1.justification: Technical disclosures are unchanged, including the supplementary-code and planned post-review release statement, and the laptop specifications of 16 GB RAM and a 2.10 GHz processor in footnote 4.

R1.justification: All 35 reference entries and the related-work discussion are retained. Reference-page reflow introduces no citation or research-positioning change.

P1.justification: v2 removes Tournesol from Gilles Bareilles's affiliation and adds an Acknowledgements paragraph identifying Horizon Europe funding under grant 101070568. The scientific prose and main-text and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block is respaced, and the new acknowledgement shifts references across pages 10–12. Figures 1–2, their captions, and the scientific-content layout remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding disclosure and adjusts an affiliation and layout, but leaves the scientific arguments, Appendices A–G, experiments, results, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged. These administrative edits do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
